About Neuralink:

We are creating devices that enable a bi-directional interface with the brain. These devices allow us to restore movement to the paralyzed, restore sight to the blind, and revolutionize how humans interact with their digital world.

Team Description:

To achieve Neuralink's mission and provide our technology to those who need it, the surgical process that implants our devices must be exceptionally safe, efficient, and scalable. The surgical robot we design is key to enabling this. The Robot Manufacturing team builds, tests, and integrates all mechanical and electrical aspects of the robot, and works closely with the electrical, mechanical, optical and software teams to take that hardware from prototype to reliable, repeatable production. This role supports manufacturing: the test fixtures, flashing stations, and quality-control tools that let us build, verify, and ship robots and robot subassemblies at scale.

Job Description and Responsibilities:

As an Electrical Test Engineer Intern, you will contribute directly to the production and scaling of Neuralink's surgical robotic systems. This role provides hands-on experience in a fast-paced, high-precision manufacturing environment, where you will own meaningful projects: designing, building, and deploying the electrical test tools and processes that improve production efficiency and ensure the quality and reliability of critical robot hardware. Your primary project will be the Minimal Robot Unit (MRU): a compact, self-contained system that drives and verifies individual robot motion stages, used at Neuralink to test stages before robot assembly and at our stage supplier as an incoming-quality check before stages ship to us. Specific responsibilities and projects may include:

- Designing, building, and bringing up the Minimal Robot Unit (MRU) to command axis motion and verify robot stage performance, including hardware, wiring, and communication software

- Developing PCBA testers, an E-Stop PCB tester, and cable continuity testers for production use

- Building PCBA flashing stations and programming setups for manufacturing

- Developing and supporting electrical automated test systems (EATS)

- Writing robot communication software and operator-facing test and diagnostic tools (e.g., MMI Studio-style applications)

- Creating Altium schematics and cable/harness drawings for test fixtures and robot cabling

- Designing camera calibration setups and fixtures

- Writing test procedures and operator documentation, and supporting deployment of test equipment to the production floor and to suppliers

- Supporting broader team efforts through debugging, failure analysis, and manufacturing support

Required Qualifications:

- Currently pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field

- Demonstrable experience developing circuits, test equipment, or products that have been used by real users; student design team work and personal projects may apply

- Circuit board design experience, including schematic capture and layout (Altium preferred)

- Software development experience in Python, C/C++, or Rust for hardware control, automation, or data acquisition

- Experience with common communication protocols (e.g., SPI, UART, I2C, CAN, EtherCAT, Ethernet)

- Competent with common lab equipment (oscilloscopes, power supplies, DMMs, etc.) and hands-on hardware debugging

Preferred Qualifications:

- A portfolio showing examples of projects you have completed

- Experience with motion control, motor drivers, or servo systems (e.g., linear stages, encoders)

- Experience building automated test fixtures, bed-of-nails testers, or production test systems

- Experience with cable and wire harness design and documentation

- Experience with embedded firmware development and device programming/flashing

- Experience with camera calibration or machine vision

- Experience building GUI or operator tools for test and diagnostics

- Experience developing electronics for critical systems in fields such as medical devices, aerospace, automotive, or military

Additional Requirements and Competencies:

- Available to work full-time, on-site in South San Francisco, starting January 2027

- Ability to lift up to 25 lb and work hands-on with robot hardware in a lab and manufacturing environment
